To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spatial pattern and density of light illumination determines the kinetics and efficiency of ChR2 stimulation.
the spatial pattern, kinetics and amplitude of illumination have a strong effect on the kinetics, efficiency and back propagation of optogenetic stimulation.
the pattern of illumination has a major impact on the spiking output of a neuron and that the irradiance threshold is a function of the ChR2 density and the degree of demyelination of the axon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of spatially patterned illumination on the response of a ChR2 expressing neuron.
the spatial pattern of stimulation and how this affects the spiking output and bAPs of ChR2 expressing neurons.
the spatial pattern of light in optogenetic stimulations, a parameter which to our knowledge has not been studied before.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spatial pattern and the intensity of illumination have a strong impact on the kinetics of the neuronal response, and hence should be carefully considered for any optogenetic experiment.
the spatial pattern and intensity of illumination can be used as a tool to modulate and probe neuronal activity.
the pattern of illumination is a key parameter to consider when using ChR2 for neuronal stimulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patterned illumination is an effective way to modulate the spiking output and the kinetics of bAPs.

spatially patterned illumination of ChR2 expressing neurons is a powerful tool for modulating the kinetics of action potentials, the efficiency of stimulation, the spiking pattern, the bAPs, and the spike time dependent plasticities, which are all critical for understanding and modulating neuronal computations and functions.
patterned illumination strategies can be used to achieve a desired spiking output, to modulate bAPs and to remotely probe the health of neural myelin.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the spatial pattern and intensity of illumination is an important consideration for the design of optogenetic experiments and that the irradiance threshold can be used as a marker to probe the health status of axonal myelination in a remote fashion.

the spatial pattern and density of ChR2 expression should be carefully considered in optogenetic experiments, as it will impact the kinetics, efficiency and reliability of stimulation and the resulting neural activity.
the spatial pattern used for optogenetic stimulation can be used to tune the response of the neurons and hence to achieve a desired outcome.
